# Frequently asked questions

Short answers to what testers ask most.

## Frequently asked questions

The fifteen questions beta testers ask most, answered plainly. Each answer ends with the code that
backs it up; the notes are at the bottom.

### 1. Does EZLM work without internet?

Yes, once a model is set up. The model runs on your computer and EZLM talks to it at a local address,
so Chat and connected apps keep working with the network off. You need internet to download the
engine and the model, to check for updates, and to send a report; if the model list cannot be
reached, EZLM uses the list built into the app.[^1]

### 2. Where are the models?

By default in EZLM's home folder, `~/.ezlm/models`, with the engine in `~/.ezlm/bin`. On Windows, if
another fixed drive has 10 GB more free space, first setup puts new models on that drive under
`EZLM\models`; Settings > Storage lets you choose another folder, and EZLM remembers every folder it
has used. A model is one or more files between about 0.5 GB and 68 GB in this beta.[^2]

### 3. Can I use my graphics card?

Yes, if it is a supported card: NVIDIA (CUDA), AMD Radeon RX or Pro and Intel Arc (Vulkan), or
Apple Silicon (Metal). EZLM picks the matching engine build and puts as many layers on the card as
fit. Ordinary built-in graphics are left out because they are about as fast as the processor, and if
a card's driver fails to load the model, EZLM retries on the processor and shows "Running on the
processor".[^3]

### 4. Why is it slow?

Speed depends on how much of the model fits in graphics memory and how fast that memory is; a model
that only partly fits, or runs on the processor, is much slower. EZLM estimates tokens per second
before setup and calls a plan slow below 8 tokens per second, or 2 on processor-only machines, and the
first answer after a start is slower while the model loads. Other apps holding graphics memory also
slow it down, and Free up memory offers to close them.[^4]

### 5. Why did it pick a smaller model than I expected?

EZLM picks the most capable model that fits in the memory left after a safety margin for the system
and other apps, so a larger model that would not fit is skipped. Balanced, Smartest and Fastest
change the trade-off; Smartest accepts a slower model but still one that fits. You can choose another
model on the Models page, which shows its speed and memory before you download.[^5]

### 6. Is it safe? Does it send anything?

While you chat, nothing leaves the computer: the model server listens on 127.0.0.1 and every request
needs the API key EZLM generated. EZLM goes online only to download, to check for updates, and to send
a problem report you asked for. A report becomes a public GitHub issue and contains what you typed in
the box plus, if you leave the box ticked, your hardware, versions and recent logs; keys and files
are never included.[^6]

### 7. Can I delete it, and what is left behind?

On Windows, Settings > Apps > Installed apps > EZLM > Uninstall asks whether to keep the downloaded
models. On a Mac, press Remove models and settings in EZLM, then drag EZLM to the Trash. Remove
models and settings deletes EZLM's home folder (engine, models, settings, keys) and any model folder
EZLM created on another drive; chats and memory are stored separately and stay until you delete their
folder.[^7]

### 8. What do I need to run it?

Windows 10 or 11 on Intel/AMD or ARM, or a Mac with Apple Silicon (M1 or later); the Windows
installer is per user and needs no admin password. Plan for 2 to 60 GB of free disk for a model and
enough memory to hold it. With little free memory EZLM picks a smaller model, down to about 0.5 GB.[^8]

### 9. Is it free? Do I need an account?

You do not need an account or a key from a service: EZLM downloads the engine from llama.cpp's GitHub
releases and the model files from Hugging Face, then gives you a local URL and key. Downloads are
checked against a published SHA-256 before EZLM runs anything.[^9]

### 10. Can I use it from other apps?

Yes, anything that speaks the OpenAI API can use it: set the base URL to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1`
and the API key to the key shown in EZLM, with the model name EZLM shows. The Connect page writes
those settings for OpenCode, Hermes and DeepSeek Harness, and checks that each one answers.[^10]

### 11. Can other devices on my network use it?

Turn on LAN mode and EZLM listens on all network interfaces, so another device can use
`http://<your-computer-ip>:<port>/v1` with the same key. That traffic is plain HTTP on your local
network, so use LAN mode only on a network you trust and turn it off when you are done. The key is
still required.[^11]

### 12. Why does Windows or macOS warn about the app?

The beta is not code-signed or notarized, so Windows SmartScreen shows "Windows protected your PC"
and macOS says it cannot verify the app; both have a path through, More info then Run anyway on
Windows, Open Anyway in Privacy & Security on a Mac. Windows 11 with Smart App Control blocks
unsigned apps outright, with no bypass. An antivirus can also quarantine the engine program; EZLM
notices and downloads it again, and allowing `~/.ezlm/bin` in the antivirus stops it repeating.[^12]

### 13. Where are my chats and memory, and how do I delete them?

On Windows they are in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\EZLM` (`chats` and `memory.md`); on a Mac in
`~/Library/Application Support/EZLM`. They never leave the computer and are not part of a model
download. Use Delete all chats in Chat, or delete the folder, to clear them; `memory.md` holds the
facts EZLM remembers about you.[^13]

### 14. Can I switch models or update without downloading everything again?

Downloaded models stay on disk, and EZLM reuses a file it already has, so going back to a model you
used before does not download it again. If the new model does not fit beside the old one, EZLM
removes the old model to make room and says so first. Updates keep your models.[^14]

### 15. Does it keep running in the background?

Yes: after setup EZLM registers the model server to start when you sign in, as a Windows startup
entry or a Mac launch agent, so it is ready when an app connects. Stop server stops it and keeps it
stopped until you press Start, and you can turn the startup entry off in Task Manager > Startup apps.
While it runs it holds the model in memory, so stop it when you need the memory back.[^15]
